summary: This short note describes Vilnius County, the largest of Lithuania's 10 counties, situated in the east of the country around the capital city Vilnius. It notes that the county administration was abolished on 1 July 2010, after which the county remained only as a territorial and statistical unit.
one_line: Vilnius County is Lithuania's largest county, located in the east around Vilnius, and has been a territorial and statistical unit since its administration was abolished in 2010.
key_facts: Vilnius County is the largest of the 10 counties of Lithuania.
Vilnius County is located in the east of Lithuania.
Vilnius County is centered around the city Vilnius.
The county administration of Vilnius County was abolished on 1 July 2010.
Since 1 July 2010, Vilnius County remains as a territorial and statistical unit.
Lithuania is divided into 10 counties, of which Vilnius County is the largest.
